name: Ifè
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.quote: Like Yoruba, Ife has three discrete level tones (H, M, L) and all vowels as well as surface pre-consonantal and final nasals are tone bearing. The Yoruba M tone has been analysed as underlyingly toneless (Akinlabi 1985; Akinlabi & Liberman 2000: 33-35), but no such analysis has yet been applied to Ife. Kohler (1983: 139, 141) finds no evidence of automatic downstep in Ife [...] indeed Kohler's Ife dataset contains no contour tones at all. || Gblem-Poidi 2018: 13: «L'ifɛ est une langue tonale, c'est-à-dire qu'elle utilise trois hauteurs mélodiques ou tons pour distinguer les mots.»
new_statements.translation: (Gblem-Poidi:) 'Ifɛ is a tone language, i.e. it uses three pitch levels or tones to distinguish words.'
new_statements.citation: Kohler, Anna; Roberts, David; Harley, Matthew; Sena, Komi. 2025. Vowel and tone processes in Ife (Togo). Studies in African Languages and Cultures 59: 61-88. doi:10.32690/SALC59.3
new_statements.locator: sec. 1.4.3 'Tone', p. 66 (phonological sketch sec. 1.4, pp. 65-67); corroborated by Gblem-Poidi 2018 sec. 3.2.3, p. 13
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote check: lines 237-261 (printed pp. 66-67, sec. 1.4.3 'Tone') carry the quoted sentences verbatim: 'Like Yoruba, Ife has three discrete level tones (H, M, L) and all vowels as well as surface pre-consonantal and final nasals are tone bearing. The Yoruba M tone has been analysed as underlyingly toneless (Akinlabi 1985; Akinlabi & Liberman 2000: 33-35), but no such analysis has yet been applied to Ife. Kohler (1983: 139, 141) finds no evidence of automatic downstep in Ife... indeed Kohler's Ife dataset contains no contour tones at all.' The Gblem-Poidi 2018 corroborating sentence is verbatim at line 301 (p. 13, sec. 3.2.3): 'L'ifɛ est une langue tonale, c'est-à-dire qu'elle utilise trois…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Ifè is described as a three-level-tone language (H, M, L; every vowel and syllabic/surface nasal is a tone-bearing unit; no downstep, no contour tones). None of the accessible descriptions (Kohler et al. 2025 phonological sketch, Gblem-Poidi 2018, Maduagwu & Dare 2016, Peace Corps 2010) says anything about word stress or accent; no stress rule can be extracted.
new_statements.domain_note: Tone described at word level and across word boundaries (V#V processes); stress/accent simply not discussed. Kohler et al. 2025 is a first-hand SIL description based on Kohler's 1980s fieldwork (Atakpamé-area Ifè, Togo) re-checked with a native-speaker co-author.
new_statements.identity_note: Target is Ifè of Togo/Benin (Ana, Ana-Ifè, Baate; ifee1241, ISO ife), an Ede/Yoruboid language — not the Ifẹ̀ dialect of Yoruba spoken at Ilé-Ifẹ̀, Nigeria (Orie 2001 'Ife Yoruba' and Salami 1986 in the Glottolog list concern the Nigerian variety and are mis-tagged). Kohler et al. 2025 rests on Kohler's 1980s SIL fieldwork in the Atakpamé area (Togo) checked by native speaker Komi Sena; Gblem-Poidi 2018 names three variants (Atakpamé town, Dassa/Datcha, Kamina); Klaver 1995 uses the Tchetti dialect (Akparè); Maduagwu & Dare 2016 describe Ifè of Bantè, Benin.

The words stress/accent (prosodic) do not occur anywhere in the article; silent on word stress.
